title: Indian-American Aman Sanger, 25, Set to Be Worth $5.5 Billion After SpaceX Acquires His AI Startup Cursor
excerpt: SpaceX agreed to acquire Anysphere, the company behind AI code editor Cursor, in a $60 billion all-stock deal — making its Indian-origin co-founder one of the youngest billionaires in tech.
body:
• SpaceX has agreed to acquire Anysphere, the company behind AI code editor Cursor, in an all-stock deal valued at $60 billion.
  • Indian-American co-founder Aman Sanger, 25, will see his estimated net worth reach $5.5 billion once the deal closes in Q3 2026.
  • Cursor has crossed $4 billion in annualized revenue and is used by millions of developers at roughly 50,000 companies, including Nvidia, Adobe, and Uber.
  • Sanger, the son of an IIT Bombay alumnus, dropped out of MIT in 2022 to co-found the startup with three classmates.

The $60 Billion Deal

Elon Musk's SpaceX has agreed to acquire Anysphere Inc. — the parent company of AI coding platform Cursor — in an all-stock merger valued at $60 billion, according to an SEC filing. The transaction, expected to close by Q3 2026, will absorb Anysphere as a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary, with Cursor shareholders converted into SpaceX Class A stock.

The deal announcement came just four days after SpaceX's record-breaking Nasdaq initial public offering, which saw shares close at $160.95 on debut day, giving the rocket maker a market capitalization of roughly $2.2 trillion.

"Excited to train some very strong models!"

— Aman Sanger, reacting to the acquisition on X

From MIT Dorm Room to Billions

Sanger, born in New York to Indian immigrant parents, began coding at age 14. His father, Arvind Sanger, is an IIT Bombay alumnus who built a career in hedge funds. His mother, Shilpa Sanger, is an orthodontist and board member of Pratham USA, the education nonprofit.

At MIT, Sanger studied computer science and mathematics before dropping out in 2022 alongside classmates Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, and Arvid Lunnemark to launch Anysphere. Before the startup, he interned at Google and Bridgewater Associates and ran an AI consultancy. He also co-authored a 2021 paper in Nature Methods on Tangram, a deep-learning framework for computational biology.

The four co-founders initially explored building an AI copilot for the mechanical engineering industry before pivoting to software engineering — a decision that proved transformative.

What Makes Cursor Different

Unlike typical coding assistants that sit alongside a developer's workflow, Cursor is designed to analyze and reason over entire codebases. It can generate code, detect bugs, and manage tasks sophisticated enough to require genuine programming expertise. The tool has become closely linked to "vibe coding" — a method where engineers build software through natural language prompts while AI handles large-scale code generation and debugging.

Cursor now serves more than 50,000 teams, including engineering organizations at Nvidia, Adobe, Uber, Shopify, and PayPal. The company claims its tools are used across 64% of Fortune 500 firms, generating up to 100 million lines of code per day, according to Outlook Business.

The growth trajectory has been staggering. Cursor crossed $1 billion in annualized revenue in November 2025 and reached approximately $4 billion in annualized revenue by early June 2026, according to multiple reports.

A Wealth Milestone for Indian-Americans in Tech

Following Anysphere's November 2025 funding round — which valued the company at $29.3 billion — Forbes estimated that all four co-founders had become billionaires. The SpaceX acquisition is projected to roughly double that wealth. NDTV Profit estimates Sanger's net worth at $5.5 billion post-deal, according to his ownership stake.

Sanger serves as chief operating officer at Anysphere, overseeing product strategy, distribution, and community building. Co-founder Truell serves as CEO, while Asif leads product development.

Sanger's rise adds to a growing roster of Indian-origin entrepreneurs shaping the AI landscape in the United States — from Sundar Pichai at Google to Satya Nadella at Microsoft. At 25, he stands out for achieving that scale at a remarkably young age.

What Comes Next

SpaceX expects to finalize the merger by Q3 2026. The acquisition signals the rocket maker's growing ambitions in artificial intelligence beyond its core aerospace business. For Cursor's developer community, the deal raises questions about how deeply the platform will integrate with SpaceX's engineering infrastructure — and whether the independent coding tool will maintain its broad enterprise appeal under new ownership.
